mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals ultra-low monetary policy, reducing discount rates and encouraging risk-taking in equity markets, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% signals the end of ultra-low monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in the end of the easing cycle.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a weakening real economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates a recession.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 1550 and RSAFS < 620000

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.5%), the S&P 500 tends to have positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to market anticipation of central bank intervention and fiscal stimulus to combat unemployment.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5%

mechanism_narrative: A level of industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 (the base year) indicates a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO > 100

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals a tight labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in inflation and tightening risks.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0%

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates a recession.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 147000 and UNRATE > 5.0%

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 270), the S&P 500 tends to have negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to market pricing in the risk of central bank tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 270
